missions.name: SLIM
missions.objective: Demonstrate high-precision pinpoint lunar landing within 100 meters of target.
missions.description: Successfully landed within 55 meters of its target rim at Shioli Crater, deploying LEV-1 and LEV-2 rovers.

missions.name: Aditya-L1
missions.launch_location: Satish Dhawan Space Centre FLP, Sriharikota, India
missions.objective: Study the solar atmosphere, chromosphere, photosphere, coronal heating, and space weather from Sun-Earth L1.
missions.description: India's first dedicated solar observatory mission stationed at Lagrange point L1, 1.5 million km from Earth.

missions.name: Chandrayaan-3
missions.launch_location: Satish Dhawan Space Centre SLP, Sriharikota, India
missions.objective: Demonstrate safe soft-landing near the lunar south polar region and roving capabilities.
missions.description: First spacecraft in human history to successfully land near the Moon’s southern polar region.

missions.name: James Webb Space Telescope
missions.launch_location: Guiana Space Centre ELA-3, Kourou, French Guiana
missions.objective: Observe the first galaxies formed after the Big Bang, stellar nurseries, and exoplanet atmospheres at Sun-Earth L2.
missions.description: Largest optical telescope in space with a 6.5-meter gold-coated beryllium primary mirror.

missions.name: Mars 2020: Perseverance
missions.objective: Seek signs of ancient life, collect cache of Martian rock cores for Earth return, test MOXIE oxygen generation.
missions.description: Exploring Jezero Crater delta and riverbed deposits while testing technologies for future human exploration.

missions.name: Mars Helicopter: Ingenuity
missions.objective: Demonstrate powered, controlled aerodynamic flight in the thin atmosphere of Mars.
missions.description: Completed 72 historic flights across 17 km of Martian terrain, far surpassing its 5-flight tech demo goal.

missions.name: Tianwen-1: Zhurong
missions.launch_location: Wenchang Spacecraft Launch Site, Hainan, China
missions.objective: Study Martian topography, soil characteristics, ice distribution, and magnetic field in Utopia Planitia.
missions.description: First Chinese Mars rover, making China the second nation to operate a rover on the Martian surface.

missions.name: InSight Lander
missions.launch_location: Vandenberg Space Force Base SLC-3E, CA, USA
missions.objective: Study the deep interior structure of Mars, measuring marsquakes, core size, and crustal thickness.
missions.description: Recorded over 1,300 marsquakes and mapped the core, mantle, and crust of Mars.

missions.name: AstroSat
missions.launch_location: Satish Dhawan Space Centre FLP, Sriharikota, India
missions.objective: Observe astrophysical objects across optical, ultraviolet, and X-ray spectral bands simultaneously.
missions.description: India's first dedicated multi-wavelength space astronomy observatory.

missions.name: Hayabusa2
missions.launch_location: Tanegashima Space Center Yoshinobu Launch Complex, Japan
missions.objective: Rendezvous with near-Earth asteroid Ryugu, deploy rovers, fire impactor, and return samples to Earth.
missions.description: Successfully returned pristine Ryugu asteroid samples to Earth in 2020; currently cruising to target 1998 KY26.

missions.name: Gaia
missions.launch_location: Guiana Space Centre ELS, Kourou, French Guiana
missions.objective: Create the most precise 3D space catalog ever made of more than a billion stars in our Milky Way galaxy.
missions.description: Stationed at Sun-Earth L2, mapping stellar positions, motions, distances, and brightness.

missions.name: Mars Science Laboratory: Curiosity
missions.objective: Determine whether Mars could have ever supported microbial life inside Gale Crater.
missions.description: Nuclear-powered science laboratory climbing Mount Sharp inside Gale Crater.

missions.name: Chandrayaan-1
missions.launch_location: Satish Dhawan Space Centre SLP, Sriharikota, India
missions.objective: Orbital survey of Moon’s topography, chemical composition, and search for water.
missions.description: India's first lunar probe, operated the Moon Impact Probe that touched down at Shackleton Crater.

missions.name: Phoenix Mars Lander
missions.objective: Study the history of water in the Martian arctic plains and evaluate habitability of permafrost.
missions.description: Touched down at Vastitas Borealis, dug into soil, and scraped direct subsurface water ice.

missions.name: New Horizons
missions.objective: First reconnaissance of the Pluto system and exploration of Kuiper Belt object Arrokoth.
missions.description: Fastest spacecraft at launch, flying past Pluto in July 2015 and Arrokoth on New Year's Day 2019.

missions.name: Rosetta
missions.launch_location: Guiana Space Centre ELA-3, Kourou, French Guiana
missions.objective: Rendezvous with Comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko, accompany its perihelion passage, and deploy lander.
missions.description: First spacecraft to orbit a comet nucleus and escort it as it approached the Sun.

missions.name: Philae
missions.launch_location: Guiana Space Centre ELA-3, Kourou, French Guiana
missions.objective: Perform the first soft touchdown on a comet nucleus and conduct surface science.
missions.description: Separated from Rosetta and performed humanity's first comet surface landing on 67P.

missions.name: Mars Exploration Rover B: Opportunity
missions.objective: Search for clues about past water and habitability across Meridiani Planum.
missions.description: Traveled an unprecedented 45.16 kilometers across the surface of Mars, operating for nearly 15 years.

missions.name: Mars Exploration Rover A: Spirit
missions.objective: Search for and characterize a wide range of rocks and soils that hold clues to past water activity in Gusev Crater.
missions.description: Explored Gusev Crater and Columbia Hills for over 6 years on a planned 90-day mission.

missions.name: International Space Station
missions.objective: Serve as a permanently crewed microgravity laboratory for international scientific collaboration.
missions.description: Continuously inhabited by international crews since November 2000, orbiting at 400 km altitude.

missions.name: Cassini-Huygens
missions.objective: Study Saturn, its spectacular ring system, and its moons in unprecedented detail for 13 years.
missions.description: Discovered active cryovolcanic plumes of water ice erupting from Enceladus and methane seas on Titan.

missions.name: Mars Pathfinder
missions.objective: Demonstrate cost-effective landing with airbags and operate the first mobile wheeled rover on Mars.
missions.description: Delivered the micro-rover Sojourner to Ares Vallis, testing Martian rocks and atmospheric conditions.

missions.name: Hubble Space Telescope
missions.launch_location: Kennedy Space Center LC-39B, FL, USA
missions.objective: Observe distant stars, galaxies, and nebulae without atmospheric distortion across UV, visible, and NIR.
missions.description: One of NASA's Great Observatories, serviced 5 times by Shuttle astronauts in Low Earth Orbit.

missions.name: Voyager 1
missions.objective: Explore Jupiter and Saturn systems, then advance into the interstellar medium.
missions.description: Currently humanity's farthest active human-made object, operating in interstellar space over 24 billion km from Earth.

missions.name: Voyager 2
missions.objective: Perform a grand tour of Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune, entering interstellar space.
missions.description: The only spacecraft to visit all four outer gas giant planets of our solar system.

missions.name: Apollo 15
missions.launch_location: Kennedy Space Center LC-39A, FL, USA
missions.objective: Longer stay on the Moon with first deployment of the Lunar Roving Vehicle for geological exploration of Hadley Rille.
missions.description: Fourth crewed lunar landing and the first of the Apollo J-missions designed for extended scientific exploration.

missions.name: Apollo 11
missions.launch_location: Kennedy Space Center LC-39A, FL, USA
missions.objective: Perform a crewed lunar landing and return safely to Earth.
missions.description: First human landing on the lunar surface. Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin spent 21.5 hours on the surface.

missions.name: Surveyor 3
missions.objective: Soft land in Oceanus Procellarum and dig trench in lunar soil with robotic scoop.
missions.description: Landed in a crater; Apollo 12 astronauts later walked to it, inspected it, and brought parts back to Earth.

missions.name: Surveyor 1
missions.objective: Demonstrate soft landing technology and gather first close-up lunar surface television images.
missions.description: First American spacecraft to achieve a soft touchdown on the Moon (Oceanus Procellarum).

missions.name: Sputnik 1
missions.objective: Place the first artificial satellite into Earth orbit and broadcast radio beeps.
missions.description: Inaugurated the Space Age and ignited humanity's push into space technology.
missions.agency_name: State Space Corporation Roscosmos / Soviet Program

equipment.name: Curiosity Rover
equipment.power: MMRTG (Multi-Mission Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator, ~110 W electrical at launch, Plutonium-238 oxide) + 2x Lithium-ion 43 Ah batteries
equipment.mobility: 6-wheel rocker-bogie suspension, machined aluminum wheels with chevron grousers, independent electric steering on 4 corner wheels; maximum design speed 0.16 km/h; >32 km traversed
equipment.robotic_arm: 2.1 m 5-degree-of-freedom robotic arm with cross-axis turret carrying percussive drill (powder extraction down to 5 cm depth), Dust Removal Tool (DRT), APXS, and MAHLI imager
equipment.autonomy: Autonomous Hazard Avoidance (AutoNav) using stereo hazard cameras (Hazcams) and visual odometry for self-directed path calculation
equipment.sample_caching: CHIMRA (Collection and Handling for Interior Martian Rock Analysis) sieving and powder distribution mechanism supplying SAM and CheMin internal analytical laboratories
equipment.purpose: Assess the past and present habitability of Gale Crater by determining whether the ancient lake environment ever possessed chemical building blocks and energy sources suitable for microbial life.
equipment.technology: Entry, Descent, and Landing (EDL) guided entry with 21.5-meter supersonic parachute and rocket-powered Sky Crane descent stage tether touchdown.
equipment.instruments: Mastcam, ChemCam laser spectrometer, SAM chemistry suite, CheMin X-ray diffraction.
equipment.communication: Direct-to-Earth X-band high-gain and low-gain antennas; UHF transceiver relaying telemetry via Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and Odyssey at up to 2 Mbps.
equipment.current_location: Gediz Vallis / Mount Sharp (Aeolis Mons), Gale Crater, Mars (4.59° S, 137.44° E)
equipment.primary_region: Mount Sharp (Aeolis Mons) foothills & Gediz Vallis channel, Gale Crater, Mars
equipment.mission_phase: Extended Science Operations (Aeolis Mons Sulfate Unit Ascent)
equipment.description: Curiosity is NASA's car-sized robotic explorer that touched down inside the 154-kilometer-wide Gale Crater in August 2012. Powered by a radioisotope thermoelectric generator, it has scaled the lower layers of Mount Sharp, reading the sedimentary rock layers like pages in a planetary history book to uncover when and how Mars transitioned from a wet, potentially habitable world into an arid desert.
equipment.legacy: Pioneered the Sky Crane landing architecture that made Perseverance possible; fundamentally proved that ancient Mars once possessed persistent habitable lake and river environments suitable for microbial life.
equipment.fate: Actively traversing the upper sulfates of Mount Sharp (Aeolis Mons); MMRTG power generation continues to provide sufficient wattage for daily science operations through the late 2020s.

equipment.name: Perseverance
equipment.power: Multi-Mission Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator (MMRTG) using plutonium-238 (~110W electrical power at landing, decaying ~few percent per year)
equipment.mobility: 6-wheel rocker-bogie mobility system; 52.5 cm machined aluminum wheels with 48 curved titanium cleats; top surface speed 152 meters per hour (0.09 mph)
equipment.robotic_arm: 2.1-meter (7-foot) 5-jointed articulated arm carrying a 45 kg turret with PIXL, SHERLOC, WATSON, rotary-percussive coring drill, and ground-contact sensor
equipment.autonomy: AutoNav vision computing allowing autonomous path selection without waiting for Earth ground-in-the-loop; Terrain-Relative Navigation (TRN) for pinpoint entry, descent, and landing
equipment.sample_caching: Adaptive Caching Assembly (ACA) located in rover belly; 43 ultra-clean titanium sample tubes with hermetic sealing mechanism for future Mars Sample Return
equipment.purpose: Investigate ancient habitability, seek potential biosignature candidates in sedimentary rocks, seal cached geological cores, and test technologies for human exploration.
equipment.technology: Terrain-Relative Navigation (TRN), Sky Crane landing system, Multi-Mission Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator (MMRTG), AutoNav self-driving coprocessor, MEDLI2 heat shield sensor instrumentation.
equipment.instruments: SuperCam, PIXL, SHERLOC Raman spectrometer, RIMFAX radar, MOXIE.
equipment.communication: X-band high-gain steerable dish antenna direct to Earth (DSN); ultra-high frequency (UHF) antenna transmitting at ~2 Mbps relay to MRO, MAVEN, and ESA TGO orbiters
equipment.operational_period: July 30, 2020 – Present (Active on Mars since Feb 18, 2021)
equipment.current_location: Western Jezero Crater rim / Lac de Charmes area (18.44° N, 77.45° E)
equipment.primary_region: Western Jezero Crater Rim / Lac de Charmes, Mars
equipment.mission_phase: Extended Science Mission (Jezero Crater Rim Campaign)
equipment.description: A car-sized robotic science rover operating inside Jezero Crater on Mars. Developed by NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, Perseverance is tasked with investigating astrobiologically relevant environments, characterizing geological processes, testing in-situ resource utilization, and caching core samples for the joint NASA-ESA Mars Sample Return campaign.
equipment.discoveries: Documented ancient deltaic conglomerates and lacustrine mudstones deposited by water 3.5+ billion years ago in Jezero Crater. Confirmed igneous intrusive floor units altered by water. Successfully generated 122 grams of breathable oxygen with MOXIE. In July 2024 at Cheyava Falls in Neretva Vallis, identified organic molecules and millimeter-sized reaction rings ('leopard spots') containing iron and phosphate—classified as a potential biosignature candidate. Biological origin remains unconfirmed; further laboratory analysis of returned samples would be required to determine whether the observed features have a biological origin.
equipment.legacy: Pioneered the first off-world aerial flight (Ingenuity helicopter), the first in-situ planetary oxygen production (MOXIE), and the assembly of the first cached planetary core library. Demonstrates autonomous planetary driving and lays foundational engineering ground for future human expeditions to Mars.
equipment.fate: Actively operating on the western Jezero Crater rim / Lac de Charmes margin. Powered by MMRTG (Multi-Mission Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator) expected to maintain electrical and thermal viability through the early 2030s.

equipment.name: Chandrayaan-1 Orbiter
equipment.purpose: Multi-spectral remote sensing and chemical mapping of the Moon.
equipment.technology: Single solar panel generating 750W, bipropellant propulsion.
equipment.instruments: TMC terrain camera, HySI hyper-spectral imager, NASA Moon Mineralogy Mapper (M3).
equipment.communication: X-band payload downlink and S-band telemetry to Indian Deep Space Network.
equipment.description: India's historic first deep space mission, revolutionizing lunar science.
equipment.discoveries: Unambiguously discovered water molecules bound in the lunar regolith and polar ice deposits.
equipment.legacy: Catalyzed the global modern race for lunar south pole exploration.

equipment.name: Hayabusa2 Spacecraft
equipment.official_name: Hayabusa2 Asteroid Sample Return & Extended Mission
equipment.dimensions: 1.0 m × 1.6 m × 1.25 m (solar array span: 6.0 m)
equipment.power: GaAs triple-junction solar arrays generating ~2.6 kW at 1 AU + ion thruster bus
equipment.mobility: 4 µ10 microwave discharge ion thrusters generating 28 mN thrust each, with hydrazine RCS thrusters
equipment.robotic_arm: Sampler Horn (1 m deployable cylinder firing 5-gram tantalum bullets at 300 m/s)
equipment.autonomy: Autonomous target marker optical tracking, laser range-finding, and touchdown thruster abort logic
equipment.sample_caching: Hermetically sealed sample capsule with 3 independent chambers for surface and subsurface asteroid grains
equipment.purpose: Rendezvous with carbonaceous C-type asteroid 162173 Ryugu, map its surface, perform kinetic impact excavation, collect surface and subsurface samples, and return them safely to Earth.
equipment.technology: Ion propulsion, kinetic impact projectile (SCI), and deployable autonomous mini-rovers (MINERVA-II) and lander (MASCOT).
equipment.instruments: Optical Navigation Cameras, TIR thermal camera, NIRS3 spectrometer, Small Impactor (SCI).
equipment.communication: High-gain parabolic antenna communicating via X-band and Ka-band to Usuda Deep Space Center and JAXA stations.
equipment.current_location: Interplanetary Heliocentric Orbit (En route to Asteroid 1998 KY26)
equipment.description: Hayabusa2 is JAXA’s flagship asteroid explorer. Launched in December 2014, it arrived at C-type near-Earth asteroid Ryugu in June 2018. Over 18 months of proximity operations, it deployed multiple surface rovers, created the first artificial impact crater on an asteroid using an explosive projectile, gathered 5.4 grams of pristine samples, and successfully delivered them to the Australian outback in December 2020.
equipment.legacy: Cemented sample-return technology as the gold standard for planetary science; delivered the purest organic-rich samples of the early solar system ever studied on Earth.
equipment.fate: Cruising in interplanetary space on the Hayabusa2# extended mission following successful Earth sample return capsule release in December 2020. Xenon ion engines active; scheduled to rendezvous with fast-rotating micro-asteroid 1998 KY26 in July 2031.

equipment.name: Cassini Orbiter
equipment.purpose: Comprehensive scientific study of Saturnian rings, moons, and magnetosphere.
equipment.instruments: Imaging Science Subsystem (ISS), Cassini Radar, VIMS spectrometer, Cosmic Dust Analyzer.
equipment.communication: 4-meter high-gain antenna communicating with NASA Deep Space Network.
equipment.description: Flagship spacecraft that orbited Saturn for 13 years and completed 294 orbits.
equipment.discoveries: Discovered liquid hydrocarbon seas on Titan and geysers of salty water erupting from Enceladus.
equipment.legacy: Dived through Saturn's rings during its Grand Finale before disintegrating into the atmosphere.

equipment.name: Hubble Space Telescope
equipment.purpose: Conduct high-resolution astronomical observations from above Earth's atmosphere.
equipment.technology: Dual solar arrays, fine guidance sensors, gyroscopes, reaction wheels.
equipment.instruments: Wide Field Camera 3 (WFC3), Cosmic Origins Spectrograph (COS), ACS, STIS.
equipment.communication: High-gain steerable microwave antennas communicating via TDRSS satellites.
equipment.description: The most celebrated telescope in human history, operating continuously for over three decades.
equipment.discoveries: Determined the age of the universe (13.8B years) and discovered the acceleration of cosmic expansion.
equipment.legacy: Revolutionized all fields of modern astronomy and space science.

equipment.name: James Webb Space Telescope
equipment.purpose: Observe the first light from early galaxies and characterize habitable exoplanet atmospheres.
equipment.technology: Foldable 6.5-meter gold-plated beryllium mirror, 5-layer tennis-court-sized sunshield, cryocooler.
equipment.communication: Ka-band high-rate transmitter communicating with Deep Space Network.
equipment.current_location: Sun-Earth Lagrange Point L2 (1.5 Million km from Earth)
equipment.description: The premier astrophysics observatory in space, seeing back to 300 million years after the Big Bang.
equipment.discoveries: Discovered the earliest known galaxies and detected carbon dioxide and methane in exoplanet atmospheres.
equipment.legacy: A crowning achievement of international collaboration between NASA, ESA, and CSA.

equipment.name: Sputnik 1 Satellite
equipment.purpose: Test radio transmitter and measure orbital drag in upper atmosphere.
equipment.technology: 58-cm polished aluminum-alloy sphere with four whip antennas, zinc-silver chemical batteries.
equipment.instruments: One-watt dual radio transmitter broadcasting at 20.005 MHz and 40.002 MHz.
equipment.communication: Continuous radio beep telemetry heard by amateur radio operators worldwide.
equipment.description: The world's first artificial satellite, sparking the global Space Race and human space exploration.
equipment.discoveries: Provided density data of the upper thermosphere from orbital drag measurements.
equipment.legacy: The historic spark that began humanity's journey into the cosmos.

equipment.name: Aditya-L1 Spacecraft
equipment.purpose: Continuous observation of the Sun's corona, flares, and space weather.
equipment.technology: Solar panels generating 1,000W, bipropellant liquid apogee motor.
equipment.instruments: VELC coronagraph, SUIT ultraviolet imager, ASPEX solar wind analyzer, PAPA plasma analyzer.
equipment.communication: X-band downlink to ISRO Telemetry, Tracking and Command Network (ISTRAC).
equipment.description: India's first dedicated space observatory studying solar coronal dynamics and space weather.
equipment.discoveries: Monitors coronal mass ejections and solar storms before they impact Earth's magnetosphere.
equipment.legacy: Provides real-time space weather alerting for satellite protection.

equipment.name: AstroSat Satellite
equipment.purpose: Multi-wavelength simultaneous observation of cosmic sources.
equipment.technology: Solar arrays generating 2,100W, reaction wheels, star sensors.
equipment.instruments: UVIT ultraviolet imaging telescope, LAXPC X-ray counter, CZTI hard X-ray imager, SXT.
equipment.communication: X-band downlink to ISRO Bangalore ground station.
equipment.description: First dedicated Indian multi-wavelength astronomy mission.
equipment.discoveries: Discovered extreme UV light from distant galaxy AUDFs01 and observed coronal emission from young stars.
equipment.legacy: Operating successfully for over 9 years, far beyond its 5-year design life.

equipment.name: Gaia Spacecraft
equipment.purpose: Ultra-high precision 3D astrometric mapping of the Milky Way.
equipment.technology: Circular deployable sunshield with solar cells, micro-propulsion cold-gas thrusters.
equipment.instruments: Two optical telescopes sharing common focal plane of 106 CCD sensors (almost 1 Gigapixel).
equipment.communication: High-bandwidth phased array antenna communicating with ESA tracking stations.
equipment.description: Constructing the largest and most accurate 3D map of our galaxy and stellar motions.
equipment.discoveries: Cataloged positions, motions, and colors for nearly 2 billion stars in the Milky Way.
equipment.legacy: Revealed the history of ancient galactic collisions that formed our home galaxy.

equipment.name: International Space Station
equipment.purpose: Inhabited orbital laboratory for scientific research, biology, and technology.
equipment.technology: Giant solar arrays spanning 73 meters generating 120 kW, Truss structure, Canadarm2.
equipment.instruments: Columbus laboratory, Destiny laboratory, Kibo module, Cupola observation dome, AMS-02.
equipment.communication: Ku-band high rate data system and S-band communications via TDRS constellation.
equipment.current_location: Low Earth Orbit (418 km altitude, 51.6° inclination)
equipment.description: The crowning jewel of human peaceful international cooperation in space.
equipment.discoveries: Hosted over 270 astronauts from 21 nations and conducted over 3,000 microgravity scientific experiments.
equipment.legacy: The longest continuous human presence in space, orbiting Earth every 92 minutes.

relics.name: Lunar Module Eagle
relics.purpose: Descent to lunar surface and touchdown platform.
relics.technology: Hypergolic rocket descent engine, aluminum honeycomb landing gear.
relics.instruments: Landing radar, seismic equipment, solar wind composition foil.
relics.communication: S-band steerable antenna and VHF transceiver.
relics.current_location: Tranquility Base, Mare Tranquillitatis, Moon (0.67408° N, 23.47297° E)
relics.description: The descent stage of Apollo 11 Lunar Module Eagle that carried Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin to the surface.
relics.discoveries: Enabled first human footsteps on another world.
relics.legacy: A permanent monument marking the inaugural landing of humanity on another world.
relics.fate: Descent stage remains preserved at Tranquility Base following July 1969 lunar liftoff; ascent stage was intentionally jettisoned into lunar orbit.

relics.name: Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle
relics.mass: 210 kg (empty Earth mass) / 35 kg on Moon; 700 kg fully laden with 2 astronauts and gear
relics.dimensions: 3.1 m length × 1.8 m width × 1.1 m height (wheelbase: 2.3 m)
relics.power: Two 36-volt non-rechargeable Silver-Zinc potassium hydroxide batteries (121 Ah capacity each, ~8.7 kWh total energy)
relics.mobility: 4 independent DC electric traction motors (1/4 hp per wheel, 10,000 rpm geared 80:1 Harmonic Drive); woven zinc-coated steel wire mesh chevron tires with titanium treads; top speed 13 km/h; 27.76 km traversed
relics.robotic_arm: None (Astronaut manual operation using geological tongs, core drills, extension handles, and scoops)
relics.autonomy: None (Astronaut manual operation via central T-handle joystick controller; dead-reckoning directional gyro odometer computer)
relics.sample_caching: Astronaut-operated sample collection bags, core sample tubes, and stowage containers mounted on the aft chassis
relics.purpose: Expand the exploration radius and payload capacity of Apollo astronauts across the rugged Hadley-Apennine lunar surface.
relics.technology: Folded into Lunar Module Falcon descent stage Quadrant 1, deployed autonomously via astronaut lanyard pulleys in under 15 minutes.
relics.instruments: High-gain dish antenna, color TV camera, 16mm movie camera, magnetometer.
relics.communication: Lunar Communications Relay Unit (LCRU) with high-gain S-band parabolic antenna for direct-to-Earth color TV and VHF low-gain antenna for astronaut suit comms.
relics.operational_period: 31 July – 02 August 1971 (3 Extravehicular Activities / 18 hr 30 min drive time)
relics.primary_region: Hadley-Apennine Valley & Hadley Rille Rim, Moon
relics.description: The Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV-001) was the first wheeled vehicle driven by humans on another celestial body. Built by Boeing and Delco Electronics, it allowed astronauts David Scott and James Irwin to venture 5 kilometers away from the Lunar Module Falcon, covering 27.76 kilometers across the Hadley-Apennine valley.
relics.legacy: Revolutionized lunar field geology by expanding surface exploration distance by a factor of ten; paved the way for all subsequent off-world rovers.
relics.fate: Parked at Station 9A, approximately 100 meters east of the Hadley Rille rim and 1.4 kilometers east of Falcon lunar module descent stage. Preserved on the lunar surface under ultra-high vacuum conditions.

relics.name: Voyager 1 Spacecraft
relics.mass: 825.5 kg (Launch mass including 105 kg science instruments)
relics.dimensions: 3.7 m diameter parabolic High-Gain Antenna dish; 13 m magnetometer boom
relics.power: 3 Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generators (RTGs, Plutonium-238 oxide, initially 470 W, currently producing ~220 W electrical)
relics.mobility: Interstellar hyperbolic solar escape trajectory at ~17 km/s (~38,000 mph, ~3.6 AU/year)
relics.robotic_arm: None (Passive instrument booms and scan platform)
relics.autonomy: Onboard Fault Protection and command-loss timer routines with dual Computer Command System (CCS)
relics.sample_caching: None (Carries the 12-inch Gold-Plated Copper Interstellar Phonograph Record)
relics.purpose: Conduct close-range reconnaissance of the Jupiter and Saturn planetary systems, then venture beyond the solar heliosphere into interstellar space.
relics.technology: Three-axis stabilized using Sun sensor and Canopus star tracker; hydrazine thrusters; 3.7-meter High-Gain Antenna communicating via S-band and X-band.
relics.instruments: Magnetometer, Cosmic Ray Subsystem, Low Energy Charged Particle instrument.
relics.communication: 3.7 m High-Gain Antenna transmitting on X-band (8.4 GHz) and S-band; signal travels over 22.5 light-hours each way to NASA Deep Space Network 70-meter dishes.
relics.current_location: Interstellar Space (Outer Heliosheath, ~163 AU / 24.4 billion km from the Sun)
relics.description: Launched in September 1977, Voyager 1 completed historic flybys of Jupiter (1979) and Saturn (1980) before heading outward along a hyperbolic trajectory out of the ecliptic plane. In August 2012, Voyager 1 crossed the Heliopause to become the first human-made object to enter interstellar space. It is the most distant operational machine in human history.
relics.legacy: Humanity’s premier interstellar emissary; carries the Golden Record with greetings in 55 languages and sounds of Earth; redefined our place in the cosmos.
relics.fate: In perpetual heliocentric hyperbolic escape trajectory into the interstellar medium (~163 AU from the Sun, moving outward at ~17 km/s). Continues transmitting in-situ particle and magnetic field data via NASA Deep Space Network; RTG electrical output expected to deplete by ~2025–2030, after which it will coast indefinitely carrying the Golden Record.

relics.name: Voyager 2 Spacecraft
relics.purpose: Reconnaissance of all four outer planets and entry into interstellar space.
relics.instruments: Planetary Radio Astronomy, Magnetometer, Cosmic Ray System.
relics.communication: 3.7-meter dish antenna communicating via DSN Canberra station.
relics.current_location: Interstellar Space (~136 AU / 20.3 billion km from the Sun)
relics.description: The only human spacecraft to explore Uranus and Neptune.
relics.discoveries: Discovered 16 new moons and multiple ring systems across outer planets.
relics.legacy: Entered interstellar space in November 2018, continuing to transmit cosmic ray data.
relics.fate: In perpetual heliocentric hyperbolic escape trajectory into the interstellar medium (~136 AU from Earth, traversing south of the ecliptic plane). Continues transmitting plasma science data via NASA Deep Space Network; RTG electrical output expected to sustain instruments through ~2026+.

relics.name: Sojourner Rover
relics.purpose: First mobile robotic explorer on Mars.
relics.technology: 6-wheel rocker-bogie mobility, solar array, lithium battery backup.
relics.instruments: Alpha Proton X-ray Spectrometer (APXS), forward stereo cameras.
relics.communication: UHF radio link to Pathfinder lander base station.
relics.current_location: Carl Sagan Memorial Station, Ares Vallis, Mars (19.33° N, 33.55° W)
relics.description: First wheeled rover on another planet, measuring only 65 cm long and weighing 10.5 kg.
relics.discoveries: Confirmed basaltic volcanic rocks resembling andesite on Mars.
relics.legacy: Established the foundational mobility archetype for Spirit, Opportunity, and Curiosity.
relics.fate: Stationary near the Carl Sagan Memorial Station landing platform in Ares Vallis. Successfully completed 83 Sols of robotic exploration and APXS geochemical measurements before communications ceased on 27 September 1997. Preserved on Mars.

relics.name: Spirit Rover
relics.power: Triple-junction GaAs solar arrays (~140 W peak) + 2x Lithium-ion batteries
relics.mobility: 6-wheel rocker-bogie mechanism; 7.73 km total distance traversed; right-front wheel jammed in 2006, dragged in reverse
relics.robotic_arm: 3-joint Instrument Deployment Device (IDD) arm carrying Mössbauer spectrometer, APXS, Microscopic Imager, and RAT
relics.autonomy: Stereo-vision hazard detection and local avoidance odometry
relics.sample_caching: Rock Abrasion Tool (RAT) grinding head for exposing unweathered rock interiors
relics.purpose: Determine whether the vast basin of Gusev Crater once held an ancient lake fed by the Ma'adim Vallis canyon network.
relics.technology: Parachute, retro-rockets, and airbag impact attenuation system inside a tetrahedral lander chassis.
relics.instruments: Pancam, Mini-TES, M├Âssbauer Spectrometer, Microscopic Imager, Rock Abrasion Tool.
relics.communication: Direct-to-Earth X-band high-gain and low-gain antennas; UHF orbital relay via Mars Odyssey.
relics.current_location: Troy sand trap, west side of Home Plate plateau, Gusev Crater, Mars (14.57° S, 175.48° E)
relics.primary_region: Columbia Hills / Home Plate, Gusev Crater, Mars
relics.description: Spirit was the first of the twin Mars Exploration Rovers to arrive at the Red Planet, touching down inside the volcanic basin of Gusev Crater in January 2004. Defying its planned 90-sol design lifetime, Spirit explored for over 6 Earth years, climbing the Columbia Hills and uncovering ancient hydrothermal hot spring deposits.
relics.legacy: Demonstrated extreme resilience in planetary exploration; proved ancient Mars had active volcanic hydrothermal systems capable of preserving biological signatures; operated for 2,210 sols (over 20 times its planned warranty).
relics.fate: Stationary at the Troy sand trap on the west side of Home Plate plateau, Gusev Crater, Mars. Embedded in soft sulphate regolith since Sol 1892; last transmission received 22 March 2010. Mission concluded by NASA on 25 May 2011 after 2,210 Sols and 7.73 km traversed.

relics.name: Opportunity Rover
relics.power: Triple-junction GaAs solar arrays (140 W peak clean sol, declining to ~100 W during dust seasons) + 2x Lithium-ion 8 Ah batteries
relics.mobility: 6-wheel rocker-bogie system with individual wheel drive; spiral flexure cleats; 45.16 km total off-world driving distance record
relics.robotic_arm: 3-joint Instrument Deployment Device (IDD) arm carrying Mössbauer spectrometer, APXS, Microscopic Imager, and Rock Abrasion Tool
relics.autonomy: Local stereo hazard avoidance algorithm (Hazcams) and visual odometry with ground-commanded waypoint navigation
relics.sample_caching: Rock Abrasion Tool (RAT) diamond-impregnated grinding bits for grinding fresh surface rock faces (in-situ analysis only)
relics.purpose: Search for and characterize a wide range of rocks and soils that hold clues to past water activity on the plains of Meridiani Planum.
relics.technology: Airbag cluster cushioned landing inside an impact crater, surrounded by protective tetrahedral lander petals.
relics.instruments: Pancam, Microscopic Imager, M├Âssbauer Spectrometer, APXS.
relics.communication: High-gain steerable X-band dish and low-gain antenna for direct-to-Earth; UHF antenna for orbital relay via Mars Odyssey and MRO.
relics.current_location: Perseverance Valley, Endeavour Crater rim, Mars (2.33° S, 354.67° E)
relics.primary_region: Endeavour Crater / Perseverance Valley, Meridiani Planum, Mars
relics.description: Opportunity touched down on Mars in January 2004 for a planned 90-day mission. Defying all expectations, the solar-powered rover operated for nearly 15 Earth years (5,111 Martian sols), traversing 45.16 kilometers across Meridiani Planum and uncovering undeniable evidence that liquid water once flowed across Mars.
relics.legacy: Holds the all-time off-world distance driving record (45.16 km); proved the long-term viability of robotic field geology on other planets; transformed humanity's understanding of Martian paleoclimates.
relics.fate: Preserved in situ in Perseverance Valley on the western rim of Endeavour Crater, Mars. Solar arrays blanketed by Martian dust during the global June 2018 dust storm; last transmission received 10 June 2018. Mission officially concluded by NASA on 13 February 2019 after 5,111 Sols and 45.16 km traversed.

relics.name: Ingenuity Helicopter
relics.purpose: First powered aircraft flight in another planet's atmosphere.
relics.technology: Carbon-fiber coaxial counter-rotating blades (2,400 RPM), solar panel, lithium-ion cells.
relics.instruments: High-res terrain camera, solar tracker, inertial measurement unit.
relics.communication: Zigbee radio communication link to Perseverance rover.
relics.current_location: Airfield Chi, Valinor Hills, Jezero Crater, Mars (18.44° N, 77.45° E)
relics.description: The Wright Brothers moment of another world; completed 72 flights totaling over 128 minutes.
relics.discoveries: Aerial scout mapping safe navigation corridors for the Perseverance rover.
relics.legacy: Opened the era of planetary aerial flight exploration.
relics.fate: Stationary at "Valinor Hills" after sustaining rotor blade damage on Flight 72 on 18 January 2024. Successfully completed 72 flights spanning 17.0 km and 128.8 flight minutes (far exceeding 5-flight tech demo goal). Now functions as a stationary long-term avionics test and surface weather monitoring station.

relics.name: Phoenix Lander
relics.purpose: Excavate and analyze water ice in the Martian arctic permafrost.
relics.technology: Solar arrays, robotic articulated trenching arm, meteorological mast.
relics.instruments: TEGA thermal analyzer, MECA microscopy/chemistry lab, SSI camera.
relics.communication: UHF link through Mars Odyssey orbiter.
relics.current_location: Green Valley, Vastitas Borealis, Mars (68.2188° N, 234.2508° E)
relics.description: First spacecraft to land in the Martian arctic permafrost zone.
relics.discoveries: Exposed subsurface white ice trenches that vaporized in sunlight, and identified perchlorate.
relics.legacy: Proved the presence of near-surface water ice in the Martian high latitudes.
relics.fate: Concluded 157 Sols of polar regolith investigation in November 2008 following declining solar power during the Martian arctic winter. Confirmed subsurface water ice and detected perchlorates. Solar panels encased by seasonal carbon dioxide ice; preserved on the northern plains.

relics.name: InSight Lander
relics.purpose: Geophysical probe studying the interior crust, mantle, and core of Mars.
relics.technology: UltraFlex solar arrays, robotic deployment arm.
relics.instruments: SEIS seismometer, HP3 heat flow probe, RISE radio experiment.
relics.communication: X-band horn antenna and UHF link through MRO and 2U MarCO CubeSats.
relics.description: Stationary geophysical station that listened to the seismic heartbeat of Mars for 4 years.
relics.discoveries: Detected magnitude-5 monster marsquakes and measured the size of Mars's molten iron core.
relics.legacy: Created humanity's first complete internal geological map of the Red Planet.
relics.fate: Concluded 1,440 Sols of planetary seismology on 15 December 2022 after extensive dust accumulation on solar arrays starved the lander of electrical power. Detected over 1,300 marsquakes and mapped the crust, mantle, and core of Mars. Preserved in situ at Elysium Planitia.

relics.name: Vikram Lander
relics.mass: 1,752 kg (including 26 kg Pragyan rover and propellant)
relics.power: Side-mounted solar panels (738 W electrical generation) + Li-Ion storage battery
relics.mobility: Stationary lander chassis with four shock-absorbing aluminum legs; executed autonomous 40 cm sub-hop re-ignition on 03 Sep 2023
relics.robotic_arm: None (Ramp deployment mechanism for Pragyan rover; ChaSTE thermal penetration probe)
relics.autonomy: Lander Hazard Detection and Avoidance (LHDA) system with real-time velocity camera and processing unit
relics.sample_caching: None (In-situ physical and seismic regolith measurements)
relics.purpose: Demonstrate safe and soft landing capability near the lunar south polar region and conduct in-situ scientific measurements of the high-latitude regolith and plasma.
relics.technology: Four 800 N throttleable liquid engines, laser altimeters, and hazard-avoidance cameras enabling autonomous touchdown.
relics.instruments: ChASTE thermal probe, ILSA seismometer, RAMBHA Langmuir probe, LRA retroreflector.
relics.communication: Direct-to-Earth X-band communication to Indian Deep Space Network (IDSN) at Byalalu; secondary relay through Chandrayaan-2 orbiter.
relics.operational_period: 23 August – 04 September 2023 (1 Lunar Day / 14 Earth Days)
relics.current_location: Shiv Shakti Point, between Manzinus C and Simpelius N craters, Moon (69.373° S, 32.319° E)
relics.primary_region: Lunar High Southern Latitude / South Polar Region
relics.description: Vikram is the ISRO lander that achieved humanity’s first successful soft landing in the lunar south polar region on 23 August 2023. Touchdown occurred at Shiv Shakti Point (69.37° S). Named after Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, the lander operated for one lunar day, deploying the Pragyan rover and executing a historic hop experiment before entering planned sleep.
relics.legacy: Made India the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon and the first to land near the lunar south pole; proved high-precision autonomous hazard-avoidance landing technology.
relics.fate: Rests at Shiv Shakti Point on the high southern lunar regolith. Successfully completed nominal 1-lunar-day mission (14 Earth days) including in-situ surface science and a successful 40 cm engine hop test on 03 September 2023. Placed into dormant sleep mode prior to lunar nightfall; preserved on the Moon.

relics.name: Pragyan Rover
relics.mobility: 6-wheel rocker-bogie mechanism with custom rim treads carrying ISRO emblem and National Emblem embossments; 101.4 meters traversed
relics.autonomy: Stereo-camera visual odometry with ground hazard avoidance and autonomous course corrections
relics.sample_caching: None (Contact and remote spectroscopy of untouched polar regolith)
relics.purpose: Conduct in-situ chemical and elemental analysis of the lunar surface rocks and soil around the landing site.
relics.technology: Two-ramp egress deployment from Vikram lander deck; direct Wi-Fi/RF link to Vikram lander.
relics.instruments: Laser Induced Breakdown Spectroscope (LIBS), Alpha Particle X-ray Spectrometer (APXS).
relics.communication: Dedicated RF link directly to Vikram lander transceiver at 2.4 GHz; telemetry relayed to Earth via Vikram.
relics.current_location: Shiv Shakti Point, high southern latitude, Moon (69.373° S, 32.319° E)
relics.primary_region: Shiv Shakti Point / Lunar South Polar Region
relics.description: Pragyan is the 26-kilogram lunar rover that rolled down Vikram’s ramp onto the lunar south polar surface on 23 August 2023. Over the course of 10 Earth days, it traversed 101.4 meters, avoiding craters and conducting the first direct spectroscopy of untouched south polar regolith.
relics.legacy: First rover to operate near the lunar south pole; provided unprecedented ground-truth geochemical data validating satellite spectral observations.
relics.fate: Parked on lunar regolith at Shiv Shakti Point, approximately 100 meters from Vikram Lander. Completed 101.4-meter traverse over 10 Earth days; safely put into sleep mode on 02 September 2023 with solar panel oriented east for sunrise; preserved in situ on the lunar surface.

relics.name: Rosetta Spacecraft
relics.mass: 3,000 kg (Launch mass including 1,670 kg fuel and 100 kg Philae lander)
relics.dimensions: 2.8 m × 2.1 m × 2.0 m central body with two 14-meter solar wings (32 m total wingspan)
relics.power: Two 14 m solar wings with high-efficiency silicon cells producing 850 W at 3.4 AU from Sun
relics.mobility: Bi-propellant thruster system; 10-year cruise covering 6.4 billion km with 3 Earth and 1 Mars gravity assists
relics.robotic_arm: None (11 onboard remote-sensing spectrometers, imagers, and dust analyzers)
relics.autonomy: Comet-environment autonomous navigation relying on star trackers and optical comet limb tracking
relics.sample_caching: None (Carried the deployable Philae lander; in-situ cometary dust collection via MIDAS and COSIMA)
relics.purpose: Rendezvous with and accompany comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko along its orbit around the Sun, deploy the Philae lander, and map the evolution of a cometary nucleus.
relics.technology: First spacecraft to orbit a comet and track its transformation through perihelion; high-efficiency low-light solar arrays.
relics.instruments: OSIRIS imaging system, ALICE UV spectrometer, VIRTIS thermal mapper, ROSINA mass spectrometer.
relics.communication: 2.2 m steerable parabolic High-Gain Antenna communicating via S-band and X-band to ESA ESTRACK network.
relics.current_location: Ma’at region pit walls, small lobe, Comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko
relics.description: Rosetta was the landmark European Space Agency mission that achieved the first orbit around a comet nucleus. Launched in 2004, it travelled for a decade across 6.4 billion kilometers before rendezvousing with comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko in August 2014. It deployed the Philae lander and studied the comet for two years as it rounded the Sun.
relics.legacy: A triumph of European space engineering; completely transformed cometary science and planetary formation models.
relics.fate: On 30 September 2016, Rosetta executed a controlled descent into the Ma’at region of Comet 67P, collecting high-resolution close-up imagery and gas measurements down to the surface before shutting down transmitters upon impact. It rests permanently on the cometary nucleus.

relics.name: Philae Lander
relics.dimensions: 0.8 m × 0.85 m × 0.85 m (tripod landing gear span: 1.0 m)
relics.power: Primary battery (60 hours operation) + solar cells recharging secondary battery
relics.mobility: Stationary lander; performed two unplanned ballistic bounces across 2 hours due to harpoon non-firing
relics.robotic_arm: SD2 (Sample, Drill and Distribution) drill mechanism and MUPUS penetrator hammering boom
relics.autonomy: Pre-programmed autonomous 60-hour first-science sequence executed after separation
relics.sample_caching: Carousel oven system for heating and pyrolyzing drilled cometary samples for COSAC gas analysis
relics.purpose: Achieve the first soft touchdown on a comet nucleus, anchor to the surface, and analyze the organic and physical properties of the cometary crust.
relics.technology: Cold gas hold-down thruster, two ice harpoons, three ice screws on landing feet, and flywheel attitude control.
relics.instruments: ├çIVA camera, ROLIS descent camera, COSAC organic chemistry suite, APXS, MUPUS thermal probe.
relics.communication: Dedicated S-band transponder communicating directly with Rosetta orbiter overhead.
relics.operational_period: 12–15 November 2014 (Primary 64-Hour Science Sequence; brief contact in June 2015)
relics.current_location: Abydos crevice, beneath rocky overhang, Comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko
relics.description: Philae was the robotic lander deployed by Rosetta on 12 November 2014. After descending for 7 hours, its anchoring harpoons and thruster failed to fire, causing it to bounce twice off the comet nucleus before coming to rest in the shadowed crevice of Abydos. It completed 80% of its planned primary science sequence on battery power before entering hibernation.
relics.legacy: First spacecraft to touch down on a cometary nucleus; delivered ground-truth measurements of primordial solar system chemistry.
relics.fate: Operated for 64 hours on primary battery power before entering hibernation on 15 November 2014. Located on 02 September 2016 by Rosetta’s OSIRIS narrow-angle camera wedged under a boulder in the shadowed terrain of Abydos. Permanently preserved on Comet 67P.

relics.name: New Horizons Spacecraft
relics.purpose: Explore the Kuiper Belt, dwarf planets, and solar system frontier.
relics.technology: Single radioisotope thermoelectric generator (RTG), hydrazine propulsion.
relics.instruments: Ralph optical/infrared imager, LORRI high-res telephoto camera, Alice UV spectrometer, SWAP.
relics.communication: 2.1-meter high-gain parabolic antenna transmitting across 50+ AU.
relics.current_location: Outer Kuiper Belt (~58 AU / 8.7 billion km from the Sun)
relics.primary_region: Outer Kuiper Belt & Heliopause Transition Zone
relics.description: Flew past Pluto at 49,600 km/h in July 2015, then visited contact binary Arrokoth in 2019.
relics.discoveries: Captured the iconic heart-shaped nitrogen glacier (Sputnik Planitia) on Pluto.
relics.legacy: Currently exploring the distant outer heliosphere boundary alongside Voyagers.
relics.fate: Traversing the outer Kuiper Belt on a hyperbolic escape trajectory at ~14 km/s. Continues conducting heliospheric, plasma, and astrophysical observations in its Second Extended Mission (KEM2); RTG power projected to support telemetry through the 2030s.

relics.name: Zhurong Rover
relics.purpose: Explore the surface topography, magnetic fields, and water ice in Utopia Planitia.
relics.technology: 4 butterfly-wing solar panels, active suspension rocker system, sub-surface radar.
relics.instruments: Navcam, Multispectral Camera, Mars Surface Magnetic Field Detector, RoPeR ground-penetrating radar.
relics.communication: UHF link through Tianwen-1 orbiter and direct X-band link.
relics.current_location: Southern Utopia Planitia, Mars (25.10° N, 109.90° E)
relics.description: First Chinese Mars rover, drove 1,921 meters across the vast northern lowlands.
relics.discoveries: Detected layered subsurface structures indicative of ancient sedimentary floods.
relics.legacy: Marks China's arrival as a major rover operator on Mars, resting in Utopia Planitia.
relics.fate: Traversed 1,921 meters across Utopia Planitia before entering planned hibernation on 18 May 2022 ahead of Martian winter. Failed to wake up in December 2022 due to heavy dust accumulation on solar arrays and extreme cold. Preserved on Mars.

relics.name: SLIM Lander
relics.purpose: Demonstrate 100-meter pinpoint landing technology on steep crater slopes.
relics.technology: Ceramic thruster engines, vision-based crater navigation, aluminum crushable landing legs.
relics.instruments: Multi-band camera, laser rangefinder, deployment systems for LEV-1 and LEV-2.
relics.communication: S-band communication link to JAXA Usuda Deep Space Center.
relics.current_location: Shioli Crater rim slope, Moon (13.3160° S, 25.2510° E)
relics.description: Achieved unprecedented pinpoint landing accuracy, touching down just 55 meters from its target.
relics.discoveries: Survived three brutal -130°C lunar nights and transmitted high-res spectroscopy of lunar olivine.
relics.legacy: Established Japan as the 5th nation to soft-land on the Moon, resting at Shioli Crater.
relics.fate: Achieved historic pinpoint landing within 55 meters of target on 19 January 2024. Successfully operated multi-band camera and survived three extreme two-week lunar nights despite resting nose-down. Final telemetry session concluded in April 2024; preserved on the Moon.

relics.name: Surveyor 3 Lander
relics.purpose: Perform soft landing and dig lunar surface with motorized scoop.
relics.technology: Throttleable vernier engines, radar altimeter, tripod landing gear with strain gauges.
relics.instruments: Television camera, surface soil mechanics sampler scoop.
relics.communication: Planar array high-gain antenna communicating with NASA DSN.
relics.current_location: Surveyor Crater, Oceanus Procellarum, Moon (3.0163° S, 23.4180° W)
relics.description: Landed in a crater; later visited by Apollo 12 astronauts Pete Conrad and Alan Bean.
relics.discoveries: Scooped trenches up to 17.5 cm deep proving soil consistency and bearing strength.
relics.legacy: The camera brought back to Earth by Apollo 12 provided valuable data on long-term lunar exposure.
relics.fate: Soft-landed on 20 April 1967; transmitted 6,315 television frames and conducted soil mechanics tests. Visited on 19 November 1969 by Apollo 12 astronauts (Pete Conrad and Alan Bean), who examined the hardware in situ and returned its television camera and scoop to Earth for materials analysis. Preserved on the Moon.

instruments.name: APXS (MSL)
instruments.purpose: Measure abundance of major, minor, and trace chemical elements in rocks and soils in direct physical contact.
instruments.description: Bombards target samples with alpha particles and X-rays from Curium-244 isotopes, detecting backscattered X-ray emissions to identify elements from sodium to strontium.
instruments.manufacturer: Canadian Space Agency / University of Guelph
instruments.specifications: Mass: 1.8 kg | Sensor head: 80 mm diameter | Radioactive source: Curium-244

instruments.name: APXS (Pragyan)
instruments.purpose: Determine elemental composition of lunar soil (Al, Si, K, Ca, Ti, Fe) using Curium-244 radioactive source.
instruments.description: Deployed close to the regolith to excite atoms via alpha radiation, measuring emitted characteristic X-rays.
instruments.specifications: Source: 244Cm | Resolution: ~150 eV at 5.9 keV | Detection: Na through Fe

instruments.name: ChaSTE
instruments.purpose: Measure vertical thermal conductivity and temperature gradient across the lunar polar regolith down to 10 cm depth.
instruments.description: Thermal penetration probe with 10 individual precision RTD temperature sensors driven by a motorized mechanism to penetrate lunar soil.
instruments.specifications: Penetration depth: up to 100 mm | Sensor count: 10 RTDs | Temperature range: -180°C to +130°C

instruments.name: ChemCam
instruments.official_name: Chemistry and Camera Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectrometer
instruments.purpose: Rapidly determine elemental composition of rocks and soils from up to 7 meters away by vaporizing microscopic spots with laser pulses.
instruments.description: Fires 1067 nm infrared laser pulses onto targets to create an ionized plasma plume, recording emission spectra across 240–853 nm wavelengths.
instruments.specifications: Mass: 5.6 kg | Laser Energy: 14 mJ per pulse | Spectral Range: 240–853 nm | Range: 1.2 to 7 meters

instruments.name: CheMin
instruments.official_name: Chemistry and Mineralogy X-Ray Powder Diffraction Instrument
instruments.purpose: Identify and quantify specific mineral phases in drilled rocks and scooped soils.
instruments.description: Directs a collimated beam of cobalt X-rays through sieved mineral powder, producing diffraction rings on a CCD detector to identify crystallographic mineral structure.
instruments.specifications: Mass: 10 kg | Power: 40 W | Co X-ray source (28 keV) | Angular range: 2° to 50° 2-theta

instruments.name: ÇIVA
instruments.purpose: Capture 360-degree panoramic stereo imagery of the cometary surface immediately surrounding the Philae landing site.
instruments.description: Six identical micro-cameras mounted around the lander perimeter and one stereoscopic camera pair providing microscopic texture views.
instruments.specifications: Sensor count: 7 micro-cameras | Mass: 1.3 kg | Captured first ground imagery from comet surface

instruments.name: COSAC
instruments.purpose: Identify complex organic and volatile molecules in the comet surface material and determine their chirality.
instruments.description: Gas chromatograph equipped with 8 capillary columns and a high-resolution time-of-flight mass spectrometer fed by the SD2 drill pyrolysis ovens.
instruments.manufacturer: Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research (MPS)
instruments.specifications: Mass: 4.5 kg | Identified 16 organic compounds including 4 nitrogen-bearing molecules on comet

instruments.name: CRS
instruments.purpose: Detect high-energy cosmic rays originating from outside the solar system.
instruments.description: High Energy Telescope System (HETS) and Low Energy Telescope System (LETS) detecting protons, helium, and heavier nuclei up to 500 MeV/nucleon.
instruments.specifications: Energy range: 0.5 to 500 MeV/nuc | Provided definitive verification of Heliopause crossing

instruments.name: DAN
instruments.purpose: Detect subsurface hydrogen, water, and hydrated minerals down to 1 meter depth beneath the rover.
instruments.description: Pulsed neutron generator fires high-energy 14 MeV neutrons into the ground and measures the time-die-away of thermalized backscattered neutrons.
instruments.specifications: Mass: 4.9 kg | Neutron output: 10^7 neutrons/pulse | Probing depth: ~1 meter

instruments.name: GCTA
instruments.purpose: Broadcast real-time color television of lunar surface exploration and LM Falcon ascent to Mission Control.
instruments.description: Pan/tilt/zoom color camera controlled remotely from Houston with 6:1 zoom ratio and vidicon tube; captured the historic live ascent of Apollo 15 LM Falcon from the Moon.
instruments.specifications: Mass: 6.8 kg | Pan range: 360° | Tilt range: -45° to +85° | Resolution: 30 fps 525 lines

instruments.name: ILSA
instruments.purpose: Detect lunar ground acceleration and seismic events generated by natural quakes, rover motion, and meteorite impacts.
instruments.description: State-of-the-art silicon micro-machined MEMS sensor measuring ground vibrations with sub-nanog acceleration sensitivity.
instruments.specifications: Dynamic range: +/- 0.5 g | Sensitivity: 100 ng/sqrt(Hz) | Bandwidth: 0.1 to 50 Hz

instruments.name: LCRU
instruments.purpose: Provide direct-to-Earth communications and television transmission independent of the Lunar Module.
instruments.description: Self-contained electronics package with steerable 3-foot parabolic high-gain antenna for live color television and low-gain helical antenna for voice and astronaut suit biotelemetry.
instruments.specifications: Mass: 25 kg | RF Output: S-band (2272.5 MHz) 10W / 2W | Direct line-of-sight to Earth

instruments.name: LECP
instruments.purpose: Measure energy, composition, and angular distribution of ions and electrons.
instruments.description: Bi-directional rotating stepper platform with solid-state detectors measuring solar wind and interstellar boundary particles from 10 keV to 30 MeV.
instruments.specifications: Mass: 7.5 kg | Power: 4.2 W | Stepping cycle: 8 positions every 192 seconds

instruments.name: LIBS (Pragyan)
instruments.purpose: Perform qualitative and quantitative elemental analysis of lunar rocks and soil around the landing site.
instruments.description: Fires high-energy Nd:YAG laser pulses onto the lunar surface to produce localized plasma, measuring characteristic emission lines to identify elemental species.
instruments.specifications: Wavelength range: 200–800 nm | Confirmed presence of Sulfur (S) on lunar south pole

instruments.name: LRV Nav Computer
instruments.purpose: Provide real-time distance, bearing, and heading back to the Lunar Module Falcon for astronaut safety.
instruments.description: Combines inputs from a directional gyroscope, four wheel-odometer pulse counters, and an astronaut-read sun shadow compass to calculate return vectors.
instruments.specifications: Mass: 7.2 kg | Power: 10 W | Distance accuracy: within 100 meters over 10 km

instruments.name: MAG
instruments.purpose: Measure weak planetary, solar, and interstellar magnetic fields.
instruments.description: High-field and low-field triaxial fluxgate magnetometers mounted along a 13-meter deployable fiberglass boom to isolate sensors from spacecraft stray fields.
instruments.specifications: Dynamic range: 0.01 nT to 2,000,000 nT | Boom length: 13 m | Active sensor in interstellar space

instruments.name: MAHLI
instruments.purpose: Acquire microscopic, true-color images of rock coatings, grains, textures, and frost.
instruments.description: Macro-focus color CCD camera mounted on the robotic arm turret capable of resolving features as small as 14 micrometers per pixel with white and UV LED illumination.
instruments.specifications: Mass: 0.38 kg | Resolution: 1600x1200 | Working distance: 21 mm to infinity | Field of view: 34° to 39°

instruments.name: Mastcam
instruments.purpose: Capture color, stereo, and panoramic images and video of the Martian terrain, geologic features, and atmospheric dust.
instruments.description: Two camera systems mounted on Curiosity's remote sensing mast with 34 mm and 100 mm focal length lenses providing multispectral visible and near-infrared imaging.
instruments.specifications: Mass: 2.8 kg | Power: 13 W | Resolution: 1600x1200 pixels | Filter positions: 8 per camera

instruments.name: Mastcam-Z
instruments.official_name: Mastcam-Z Mast-Mounted Multispectral Stereoscopic Imaging System
instruments.purpose: Principal science cameras providing 3D stereoscopic imaging, multispectral zoom photography, and panoramic terrain characterization.
instruments.description: Dual zoom cameras mounted on the rover remote sensing mast separated by 24.2 cm. Zooms from 26 mm to 110 mm with focus from 1 meter to infinity, detecting 11 science color bands.
instruments.manufacturer: Malin Space Science Systems / Arizona State University
instruments.specifications: Resolution: 1600×1200 pixels; Focal length: 26–110 mm (4× optical zoom); Mass: 4.0 kg; Power: 17.4 W; Color bands: 11 multispectral filters (400–1000 nm).

instruments.name: MEDA
instruments.purpose: Continuous measurement of weather, ambient temperature, pressure, wind velocity, relative humidity, solar radiation, and airborne dust properties.
instruments.description: A distributed environmental sensor station across the rover mast, deck, and interior. Records diurnal atmospheric cycles, characterization of airborne dust particle shapes, optical depth, and ground thermal heat balance.
instruments.specifications: Sensors: 5 air temperature sensors, 2 wind sensors, relative humidity sensor, thermal infrared ground sensor, barometer, radiation and dust sensor (RDS); Mass: 5.5 kg; Power: 17 W.

instruments.name: Mini-TES
instruments.purpose: Determine mineral composition of surrounding rocks and soils from distances up to hundreds of meters.
instruments.description: Michelson interferometer operating across 5 to 29 micrometers thermal infrared spectrum to identify carbonates, silicates, sulfates, and hematite.
instruments.specifications: Mass: 2.1 kg | Spectral range: 339 to 1997 cm^-1 | Field of view: 20 mrad

instruments.name: Mössbauer Spectrometer
instruments.purpose: Determine oxidation state and mineralogical composition of iron-bearing minerals in rocks and soils.
instruments.description: Uses a Cobalt-57 radioactive source to excite iron-57 nuclei, measuring resonance absorption velocity spectra.
instruments.specifications: Mass: 0.5 kg | Source: 57Co | Velocity drive: +/- 10 mm/s

instruments.name: MOXIE
instruments.official_name: Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment
instruments.purpose: Technology demonstration of extracting breathable molecular oxygen (O2) from the carbon dioxide (CO2) atmosphere of Mars.
instruments.description: Draws in thin Martian atmospheric air, compresses it to 1 atm, and heats it to ~800°C within a Solid Oxide Electrolyzer Cell (SOEC) to split CO2 into oxygen and carbon monoxide. Completed 16 successful runs producing 122 grams of oxygen before planned mission conclusion in 2023.
instruments.manufacturer: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) / NASA JPL
instruments.specifications: Production rate: 6–12 grams O2 per hour (98% purity); Operating temperature: ~800°C; Mass: 17.1 kg; Power: ~300 W.

instruments.name: MUPUS
instruments.official_name: Multi-Purpose Sensors for Surface and Sub-Surface Science
instruments.purpose: Measure mechanical strength, thermal conductivity, and temperature profile of the comet nucleus crust.
instruments.description: Includes a deployable motorized hammer and sensor penetrator with 16 RTD thermal sensors driven into the comet surface.
instruments.specifications: Impact energy: adjustable up to 2 Joules | Proved comet subsurface was as hard as solid rock

instruments.name: NIRS3
instruments.purpose: Detect hydrated minerals, organic matter, and water ice on Ryugu across the 1.8 to 3.2 micrometer absorption band.
instruments.description: Cooled InGaAs array sensor measuring asteroid surface reflectance to map hydroxyl (O-H) mineral distribution.
instruments.specifications: Spectral range: 1.8 to 3.2 µm | Spectral resolution: 18 nm | Field of view: 0.1°

instruments.name: ONC-T / ONC-W
instruments.purpose: Map asteroid Ryugu in high resolution, guide precision touchdowns, and analyze spectral absorption bands.
instruments.description: ONC-T features 7 bandpass filters from 390 nm to 550 nm; ONC-W provides wide-angle context during proximity operations.
instruments.manufacturer: JAXA / University of Tokyo / Kochi University
instruments.specifications: Resolution: 1024x1024 CCD | Filters: ul, b, v, Na, w, x, p | Ground resolution: <1 mm/pixel at touchdown

instruments.name: OSIRIS
instruments.official_name: Optical, Spectroscopic, and Infrared Remote Imaging System
instruments.purpose: Map the nucleus of Comet 67P, identify active gas/dust jet vents, and locate the Philae lander on the surface.
instruments.description: Consists of a Narrow Angle Camera (NAC) for high-resolution nucleus topography and a Wide Angle Camera (WAC) for wide-field coma monitoring.
instruments.manufacturer: Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research (MPS)
instruments.specifications: Resolution: 2048x2048 CCDs | 12 filters per camera | Resolving power: centimeters per pixel from orbit

instruments.name: Pancam
instruments.purpose: Examine Martian mineralogy, atmosphere, and surface morphology in high-resolution stereo color.
instruments.description: Twin digital cameras mounted on the rover mast separated by 30 cm baseline with 8-position filter wheels spanning 400 to 1,000 nm.
instruments.specifications: Mass: 0.75 kg per camera | 1024x1024 frame transfer CCD | Angular resolution: 0.27 mrad/pixel

instruments.name: PIXL
instruments.purpose: Fine-scale elemental chemical composition mapping of abraded rock surfaces and salt crusts.
instruments.description: Mounted on the robotic arm turret. Directs an ultra-fine 120-micrometer X-ray beam at target rocks to detect and quantify 20+ chemical elements from sodium through uranium, matching elemental chemistry directly with sub-millimeter rock textures.
instruments.specifications: Beam spot: 0.12 mm diameter; Energy range: 0.9 to 28 keV; Spatial step size: down to 50 micrometers; Mass: 4.3 kg (turret sensor head) + 1.6 kg (chassis electronics); Power: ~25 W.

instruments.name: PWS
instruments.purpose: Measure plasma wave oscillations, electron densities, and shockwaves in planetary magnetospheres and the interstellar medium.
instruments.description: Two 10-meter whip antennas mounted in a V-formation connected to a 16-channel step-frequency receiver measuring plasma oscillations from 10 Hz to 56 kHz.
instruments.specifications: Antennas: 2x 10 m beryllium copper whips | Frequency: 10 Hz to 56 kHz | Recorded interstellar plasma sounds

instruments.name: RAMBHA-LP
instruments.official_name: Radio Anatomy of Moon Bound Hypersensitive Ionosphere and Atmosphere
instruments.purpose: Measure near-surface lunar plasma electron density and temperature variations across the lunar day.
instruments.description: Deployable 5 cm spherical metallic sensor held on a 1-meter boom to measure plasma currents in the sunlit lunar boundary layer.
instruments.specifications: Probe diameter: 50 mm | Bias voltage: -12V to +12V | Electron density range: 10^2 to 10^6 cm^-3

instruments.name: RAT
instruments.purpose: Grind away dust and weathered exterior rock coatings to expose unweathered rock interiors for spectrometers.
instruments.description: High-speed diamond-matrix cutting wheels driven by electric motors to create a 45 mm diameter circular pit up to 5 mm deep.
instruments.specifications: Mass: 0.7 kg | Diameter: 45 mm | Depth: up to 5 mm | Speed: 3,000 RPM

instruments.name: REMS
instruments.purpose: Record daily and seasonal cycles of atmospheric pressure, humidity, UV radiation, wind speed, and air/ground temperatures.
instruments.description: Two booms mounted on the mast measure horizontal and vertical winds, air temperature, and humidity, while deck sensors record UV flux and pressure.
instruments.specifications: Mass: 1.3 kg | Sampling rate: 1 Hz | Wind range: 0 to 70 m/s | Pressure accuracy: 3 Pa

instruments.name: RIMFAX
instruments.official_name: Radar Imager for Mars' Subsurface Experiment
instruments.purpose: Centimeter-scale structural imaging of geologic layers, buried crater rims, and structural strata beneath the rover up to 10+ meters deep.
instruments.description: Ultra-wideband frequency-modulated ground-penetrating radar with an antenna mounted on the rover's lower rear exterior. Transmits electromagnetic pulses into the Martian regolith as the rover drives, providing continuous vertical cross-sections of subsurface strata.
instruments.manufacturer: Forsvarets forskningsinstitutt (FFI / Norwegian Defence Research Establishment, Norway)
instruments.specifications: Frequency range: 150 to 1200 MHz; Penetration depth: >10 meters in dry basalt; Vertical resolution: 15–30 cm; Mass: ~3 kg; Power: 5–10 W.

instruments.name: ROMAP
instruments.official_name: Rosetta Lander Magnetometer and Plasma Monitor
instruments.purpose: Measure magnetic fields and plasma environment on the surface of Comet 67P.
instruments.description: Triaxial fluxgate magnetometer mounted on a 60 cm sensor boom; proved that Comet 67P has no measurable global magnetic field.
instruments.specifications: Magnetic range: +/- 2,000 nT | Resolution: 12 pT | Confirmed unmagnetized comet nucleus

instruments.name: ROSINA
instruments.official_name: Rosetta Orbiter Spectrometer for Ion and Neutral Analysis
instruments.type: Cometary Gas & Isotope Mass Spectrometer Suite
instruments.purpose: Determine composition and isotopic ratios of volatiles outgassing from Comet 67P's nucleus.
instruments.description: Double Focusing Mass Spectrometer (DFMS), Reflectron-type Time-of-Flight (RTOF) mass spectrometer, and Comet Pressure Sensor (COPS).
instruments.specifications: Mass resolution: m/delta-m > 3000 | Discovered D/H ratio 3x Earth oceans & molecular O2

instruments.name: SAM
instruments.official_name: Sample Analysis at Mars Instrument Suite
instruments.purpose: Search for carbon-containing organic compounds, measure light isotope ratios, and determine atmospheric composition.
instruments.description: Contains a Quadrupole Mass Spectrometer (QMS), Gas Chromatograph (GC), and Tunable Laser Spectrometer (TLS) fed by a 74-cup pyrolysis carousel heating samples up to 1,000°C.
instruments.manufacturer: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center / CNES
instruments.specifications: Mass: 40 kg | Power: 80 W | 74 sample cups | Oven range: ambient to 1,000°C

instruments.name: SCI
instruments.purpose: Create an artificial impact crater on asteroid Ryugu to expose and sample unweathered subsurface material.
instruments.description: Free-flying explosive kinetic weapon that detonate a 4.5 kg octogen shaped charge, accelerating a 2.5 kg pure copper liner into Ryugu at 2 km/s.
instruments.specifications: Projectile: 2.5 kg copper plate | Explosive: 4.5 kg Octogen | Impact velocity: 2.0 km/s | Created 10m crater

instruments.name: SHERLOC
instruments.official_name: Scanning Habitable Environments with Raman & Luminescence for Organics & Chemicals
instruments.purpose: Detection and spatial mapping of organic carbon molecules and minerals altered by aqueous environments.
instruments.description: Mounted on the arm turret, uses a deep-ultraviolet (248.6 nm) laser to excite native fluorescence and resonance Raman scattering from organic compounds without destroying the sample. Paired with WATSON (Wide Angle Topographic Sensor for Operations and eNgineering) camera for micro-scale imaging.
instruments.specifications: Laser wavelength: 248.6 nm pulsed DUV; Spatial resolution: 50-micrometer laser footprint; Context imaging: WATSON 10-micron scale; Mass: 3.11 kg (turret head) + 1.61 kg (electronics); Power: 48.8 W.

instruments.name: SuperCam
instruments.official_name: SuperCam Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy, Raman, and Luminescence Suite
instruments.purpose: Remote chemical, mineral, and atomic composition analysis of rocks and soils from up to 7 meters away.
instruments.description: Fires an infrared laser to vaporize microscopic rock points into glowing plasma (LIBS), analyzing emitted light. Features a green laser for remote Raman spectroscopy, a microphone to record laser acoustic shockwaves and Martian wind sounds, and an infrared spectrometer.
instruments.manufacturer: Los Alamos National Laboratory (USA) / IRAP / CNES (France)
instruments.specifications: Range: 7 meters (LIBS), infinite (passive VISIR); Wavelengths: 1064 nm (pulsed IR) & 532 nm (green laser); Microphone: electret condenser (100 Hz–10 kHz); Mass: 10.6 kg; Power: 17.9 W.

instruments.name: The Golden Record
instruments.official_name: The Sounds of Earth Interstellar Phonograph Record
instruments.purpose: Preserve a message of human existence, culture, and Earth biology for potential extraterrestrial discovery.
instruments.description: 12-inch gold-plated copper phonograph disc protected by an electroplated aluminum cover containing 115 analog images, greetings in 55 languages, 90 minutes of world music, and nature sounds.
instruments.manufacturer: NASA / Carl Sagan Committee / Voyager Project
instruments.specifications: Diameter: 30 cm | Material: Gold-plated copper with uranium-238 clock | Estimated lifetime: >1 billion years

instruments.name: VIRTIS
instruments.official_name: Visible and Infrared Thermal Imaging Spectrometer
instruments.purpose: Map composition, temperature distribution, and organic compounds on the comet surface.
instruments.description: Combines a visible spectrometer, near-infrared spectrometer, and high-resolution infrared sub-assembly.
instruments.specifications: Spectral range: 0.25 to 5.0 µm | Temperature sensitivity: 50 K to 400 K
